def q3_pairs(mask: int):
    pairs = {(0, q3_leaf_error(mask))}

### 4.1 W7-SOL-MDC-RANK-AREA

Let a binary linear visible handle be \(Z=AX\), with kernel \(K=\ker A\). For a coordinate set \(Q\), define
\[
r_K(Q)=\dim \pi_Q(K).
\]
Conditioned on \(Z=z\), X is uniform on an affine coset \(x_0+K\), so \(X_Q\) is uniform on \(\pi_Q(x_0)+\pi_Q(K)\). Therefore
\[
H(X_Q\mid Z,Q)=r_K(Q).
\]
Every exact binary prefix-free residual message has expected length at least this entropy. Sending coordinates in a basis of \(\pi_Q(K)\) attains it. Thus the exact residual payload for Q is \(r_K(Q)\).

Let \(Q_k=\{S_1,\ldots,S_k\}\). The carried-token schedule then gives
\[
A_K^{(m)}=\mathbb E\sum_{k=1}^m r_K(Q_k),\qquad
B_K^{(m)}=\mathbb E r_K(Q_m),
\]
\[
M_K^{seq}=(m+1)(1+h)+(1+q)A_K^{(m)},
\]
\[
L_K^{seq}=1+h+c_0+(1+q+c_1)B_K^{(m)},\qquad D_K=0.
\]
This is one common accounting law, not a candidate identification.

For \(U_{1,n}\), \(r(Q)=1\) for nonempty Q, so \(A=m,B=1\), giving
\[
(M,D,L)=(3m+2,0,4).
\]
For \(U_{n,n}\), \(r(Q)=|Q|\). At m=2,
\[
\mathbb E|Q_1|=1,\qquad \mathbb E|Q_2|=2-p_c,
\]
so \(A=3-p_c,B=2-p_c\), giving exactly
\[
(M,D,L)=\left(9-p_c,0,{11\over2}-{3p_c\over2}\right).
\]
For n >= 3, \(U_{n-1,n}\) has the same ranks for \(|Q|\le2\), hence the same two-demand ledger, but not the same handle leakage.

### 4.2 W7-SOL-MDC-UNIFORM-STRAT

Restrict to positive ranks \(1\le r\le n\). A subspace K realizes \(U_{r,n}\) exactly when a generator matrix G for K has every set of at most r columns independent, equivalently every r by r minor is nonzero.

For \(2\le r\le n-2\), put G in systematic form \([I_r\mid C]\). Any extra column must have every coordinate nonzero: if coordinate i were zero, that column together with all systematic columns except \(e_i\) would be dependent. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), the only all-nonzero column is \(\mathbf1^r\), so there can be at most one extra column. Hence \(n\le r+1\), contradicting \(r\le n-2\). Therefore no intermediate positive-rank stratum exists.

The survivors are constructive:

- r=1: \(K=\langle\mathbf1^n\rangle\), realizing \(U_{1,n}\).
- r=n-1: generator \([I_{n-1}\mid\mathbf1]\), the even-weight subspace, realizing \(U_{n-1,n}\).
- r=n: \(K=\mathbb F_2^n\), realizing \(U_{n,n}\).

The EC boundary search gives max n = 3,4,5 for fixed r = 2,3,4. The omitted rank-zero stratum is \(K=\{0\}\); it is outside the positive-residual MDC comparison.

### 4.5 W7-SOL-MDC-NONRED-FK and -KF

An **admissible handle morphism** may randomized-postprocess the existing visible handle using public randomness \(U\perp X\); may not introduce new source-dependent pre-demand information; and must preserve the registered exact residual service/rank budget.

### W7-SOL-BP1-UNIFORM-SIZE-DP [DR]

At uniform demand define

    Phi(A)=sum_i |sum_{x in A} (-1)^(x_i)|.

Then E(A)=(n|A|-Phi(A))/2. Let beta_n(k)=max_{|A|=k} Phi(A). The exact Kimi identity re-derives as follows:

    Phi(A)=max_{sigma in {+1,-1}^n} sum_{x in A} <sigma,(-1)^x>.

For fixed |A|=k, choose the k largest scores. Every sigma has the same multiset

    q_n = {n-2j repeated C(n,j) times, j=0,...,n}.

Thus beta_n(k) is exactly the sum of the k largest q_n values. Put M_n=max_k beta_n(k)=beta_n's positive-score sum and c_n=M_n/N. This also gives e1=1/2-M_n/(nN).

    D_n(a,b) := 2 M_n(a+b) + N beta_n(a+b)

    H(T_A)=sum_{leaf C below A} Phi(C)-2c_n L(T_A).

At a leaf, H=Phi(A)<=beta_n(k). If A splits into sizes a,b, induction and (C) give

    H(T_A)<=beta_n(a)+beta_n(b)-2c_n(a+b)<=beta_n(k).

At Omega, beta_n(N)=0, hence sum_leaf Phi<=2c_n L. Therefore

    e(T)=1/2-sum_leaf Phi/(2nN)
        >=1/2-[M_n/(nN)] [L/N]

## 4. n=5 heavy vertex audit and expanded root fragment

At Q5-down, w=(9,4,4,4,4), d=25, N=32, E0=400. Exact enumeration of all 2^31 canonical one-bit splits gives E1=242, e1=121/400, s1=79/400, c=s1*d=79/16, and candidate tau1=800/79. There are exactly 16 optimal root bipartitions.

For a cell C define the exact cell DP

    U_c(C)=min(E(C), min_{B disjoint D=C} c|C|+U_c(B)+U_c(D)).

In integer scaling S=32,K=158, U_c(C)=32E(C) means that every subtree under C has nonpositive excess R(C)=max[G_C-cL_C]. For root split B,C, set

    gamma=E0-E(B)-E(C),  slack=cN-gamma=158-gamma.

If R(B)+R(C)<=slack, every tree under that root satisfies the BP1 tangent.

| heavy-coordinate halfcube | 1 | 16 | 128 | 144 | 14 | R=0 on both sides |

The 16 canonical optimal masks are 00017fff, 0002bfff, 0004dfff, 0008efff, 0010f7ff, 0020fbff, 0040fdff, 0080feff, 0100ff7f, 0200ffbf, 0400ffdf, 0800ffef, 1000fff7, 2000fffb, 4000fffd, and 7fff0001. The 37 bipartitions are distinct. XOR translation preserves E and the cell DP, so one ball/coball calculation covers all 16 center-pairs; permutations of the four light coordinates cover all light-coordinate roots. For every tree whose first split is in this union, arbitrary recursive subtrees below both children satisfy the tangent at s1=79/400. The side DPs also remain at their leaf values at K=157,S=32, which is normalized side-slope s1-1/800 and independently confirms the reported side margin.

This strictly enlarges the inherited n=5 optimal-root fragment. It does not close Q5-down: suboptimal roots outside these 37 classes can have children with positive excess, and the full root slack-versus-excess inequality has not been checked over all 2^31 roots.

## 5. All-n survivors and infinite obstructions

### W7-SOL-BP1-ALLN-BASE4 [DR]

For arbitrary nonnegative weights, the W6 bias induction gives

    sum_leaf Phi_w(A) <= d L(T),
    e(T) >= 1/2-ell(T)/2.

Hence F(t)=2+t/2 on 0<=t<=4 for every n and demand class. This is a lower bound on the first breakpoint, not BP1 unless the one-bit candidate equals 4.

### W7-SOL-BP1-ANTI-LOCAL-OBSTRUCTION [DR]

For every full-support class and n>=2, an antipodal pair A={x,bar x} has E(A)=d and splitting it into singletons gains d, so its normalized split-gain density is exactly 1/2. Since e1>0, s1<1/2. Therefore any proof demanding local gain density <=s1 at every split fails for infinitely many n and for 2^(n-1) cells at each n. This blocks only edgewise greedy induction, not BP1.

### W7-SOL-BP1-LEAF-INFO-OBSTRUCTION [DR]

At the heavy vertex v_n=((n+4),4,...,4)/(5n), take A=Omega minus one point. Its posterior advantage is 1/[2(N-1)], so advantage divided by self-information is

    R_n = 1 / [2(N-1) log2(N/(N-1))] > ln(2)/2 > 1/3.

Fourier Cauchy-Parseval gives s1<=||v_n||_2/2 with ||v_n||_2^2=(n+24)/(25n), hence s1<=3/10<1/3 for n>=3. Thus the pointwise leaf budget advantage<=s1 log2(N/|A|) fails for every n>=3. This blocks leafwise self-information charging, not sibling-coupled or global potentials.

A corrected trivial depth fragment is also exact: if every leaf has depth at least r, then G/(dL)<=1/(2r). It certifies such trees only when s1>=1/(2r). For Q5-down, r=3 works because 1/6<79/400; r=2 does not follow from this bound.

  ## 3. No-message and all-\(n\) tail
  
  Put \(K_m=|\{S_1,\ldots,S_m\}|\). For every deterministic \(r\)-leaf realization,
  \[
  \boxed{P_T\le\mathbb E_\theta\min\{1,r2^{-K_m}\}.}\tag{3.1}
  \]
  Conditional on \(K_m=k\), answers leave at most \(2^{n-k}\) compatible words per leaf, hence at most \(\min(2^n,r2^{n-k})\) successful words. For \(r=1\), a prototype attains
  \[
  \boxed{P_{0,m}(\theta)=\mathbb E2^{-K_m}=2^{-n}\sum_{B\subseteq[n]}\theta(B)^m.}\tag{3.2}
  \]
  This is symmetric convex/Schur-convex, maximized over \(\Theta_n^\downarrow\) at \(v_n\). Thus
  \[
  p_{n,m}={1\over2^n(5n)^m}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}{n-1\choose k}[(n+4+4k)^m+(4k)^m],
  \quad G_0(n,m)=40(1-p_{n,m})-(2m+1).\tag{3.3}
  \]
  For \(m\ge10\),
  \[
  p_{n,m}-p_{n,m+1}=\mathbb E[Z^m(1-Z)]\le m^m/(m+1)^{m+1}<1/20,
  \quad\boxed{20m^m<(m+1)^{m+1}},\tag{3.4}
  \]
  so \(G_0(n,m)>G_0(n,m+1)\).
  
  | \(n\) | last + \(m\): exact \(G_0\) | first - \(m\): exact \(G_0\) |
  |---:|---:|---:|

  ## 4. n=5 heavy vertex audit and expanded root fragment
  
  At Q5-down, w=(9,4,4,4,4), d=25, N=32, E0=400. Exact enumeration of all 2^31 canonical one-bit splits gives E1=242, e1=121/400, s1=79/400, c=s1*d=79/16, and candidate tau1=800/79. There are exactly 16 optimal root bipartitions.
  
  For a cell C define the exact cell DP
  
      U_c(C)=min(E(C), min_{B disjoint D=C} c|C|+U_c(B)+U_c(D)).
  
  In integer scaling S=32,K=158, U_c(C)=32E(C) means that every subtree under C has nonpositive excess R(C)=max[G_C-cL_C]. For root split B,C, set
  
      gamma=E0-E(B)-E(C),  slack=cN-gamma=158-gamma.
  
  If R(B)+R(C)<=slack, every tree under that root satisfies the BP1 tangent.
  
  ### W7-SOL-BP1-Q5DOWN-ROOT37 [DR|EC]
  
  | first-split family | canonical roots | |side| | E per side | gamma | slack | cell DP at K=158 |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
  | exact one-bit optimizers, masks beginning 0x00017fff,... | 16 | 16 | 121 | 158 | 0 | R=0 on all 32 sides |
  | radius-2 Hamming balls versus coballs | 16 | 16 | 125 | 150 | 8 | R=0 on all sides |
  | heavy-coordinate halfcube | 1 | 16 | 128 | 144 | 14 | R=0 on both sides |
  | light-coordinate halfcube | 4 | 16 | 168 | 64 | 94 | R=0 on all 8 sides |
  
  The 16 canonical optimal masks are 00017fff, 0002bfff, 0004dfff, 0008efff, 0010f7ff, 0020fbff, 0040fdff, 0080feff, 0100ff7f, 0200ffbf, 0400ffdf, 0800ffef, 1000fff7, 2000fffb, 4000fffd, and 7fff0001. The 37 bipartitions are distinct. XOR translation preserves E and the cell DP, so one ball/coball calculation covers all 16 center-pairs; permutations of the four light coordinates cover all light-coordinate roots. For every tree whose first split is in this union, arbitrary recursive subtrees below both children satisfy the tangent at s1=79/400. The side DPs also remain at their leaf values at K=157,S=32, which is normalized side-slope s1-1/800 and independently confirms the reported side margin.

  ## 5. All-n survivors and infinite obstructions
  
  ### W7-SOL-BP1-ALLN-BASE4 [DR]
  
  For arbitrary nonnegative weights, the W6 bias induction gives
  
      sum_leaf Phi_w(A) <= d L(T),
      e(T) >= 1/2-ell(T)/2.
  
  Hence F(t)=2+t/2 on 0<=t<=4 for every n and demand class. This is a lower bound on the first breakpoint, not BP1 unless the one-bit candidate equals 4.
  
  ### W7-SOL-BP1-ANTI-LOCAL-OBSTRUCTION [DR]
  
  For every full-support class and n>=2, an antipodal pair A={x,bar x} has E(A)=d and splitting it into singletons gains d, so its normalized split-gain density is exactly 1/2. Since e1>0, s1<1/2. Therefore any proof demanding local gain density <=s1 at every split fails for infinitely many n and for 2^(n-1) cells at each n. This blocks only edgewise greedy induction, not BP1.
  
  ### W7-SOL-BP1-LEAF-INFO-OBSTRUCTION [DR]
  
  At the heavy vertex v_n=((n+4),4,...,4)/(5n), take A=Omega minus one point. Its posterior advantage is 1/[2(N-1)], so advantage divided by self-information is
  
      R_n = 1 / [2(N-1) log2(N/(N-1))] > ln(2)/2 > 1/3.
  
  Fourier Cauchy-Parseval gives s1<=||v_n||_2/2 with ||v_n||_2^2=(n+24)/(25n), hence s1<=3/10<1/3 for n>=3. Thus the pointwise leaf budget advantage<=s1 log2(N/|A|) fails for every n>=3. This blocks leafwise self-information charging, not sibling-coupled or global potentials.
  
  A corrected trivial depth fragment is also exact: if every leaf has depth at least r, then G/(dL)<=1/(2r). It certifies such trees only when s1>=1/(2r). For Q5-down, r=3 works because 1/6<79/400; r=2 does not follow from this bound.
